- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment oscillates (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation); model often fails to revert; apply smoothing to forecast mean by 1–3% toward prior 10d average.
- When official events are clustered (e.g., 3+ auctions in 30d), model overfits to recent supply shocks; reduce forecast volatility by 15–25% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underperforms; increase forecast baseline by 1–3% to account for latent volatility.
